name: Wild Places Worth Keeping
description: The first national parks and the reserves that followed, from Yellowstone to Virunga, and the lands left to nature after human disaster.

checkpoints.name: Parks and gardens
checkpoints.note: Before nature reserves there were parks for people. Hyde Park opened to the public, Kew collected plants from the empire, and New York built Central Park for crowded city dwellers.

checkpoints.name: The first national parks
checkpoints.note: Yellowstone began the idea that land could be kept for everyone. Australia, Canada and the United States followed, and Africa's first national park, in the Congo, came in 1925.

checkpoints.name: The idea goes global
checkpoints.note: Africa and South America created parks for elephants, lions and waterfalls. The Serengeti and the Galapagos showed that parks could protect migrations and species found nowhere else.

checkpoints.name: Conservation and recovery
checkpoints.note: Rhinos recovered in Chitwan, a vast reef park was set up in Australia and the Himalayas gained protection. At Chernobyl, wildlife moved back into the land people left.
